newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF asked banks to help NCB restructuring - bankers.
newsitem.headline: MOF asked banks to help NCB restructuring - bankers.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) asked commercial banks if they would help out Nippon Credit Bank in its efforts at restructuring, banking sources said on Thursday.

They said a senior MOF official visited their offices asking them if they would want to buy new shares to be issued by NCB in order to boost the ailing bank's capital. They said they did not give a reply.

A newspaper report on Thursday said that under consideration was the use of 80 billion to 90 billion yen from a fund set up to help clean up failed mortgage firms to buy newly issued NCB shares which would then be sold to private financial institutions.
A senior MOF official told Reuters he could not comment.
"I cannot comment on that. There is no way to confirm that. But we do exchange views with banks on various issues and the topic of NCB could be one of them," he added.
The sources said the MOF official hinted that the request would be made to the 20 Japanese major banks excluding NCB.
They also quoted the official as saying NCB's restructuring plan would include steps such as shutting down some overseas branches and sales of real estate including its Tokyo headquarters.
The newspaper report also said the bank was going to withdraw from overseas operations and to post losses for two consecutive years was mere speculation.
NCB said at a news conference that the report was mere speculation.
